x: After 2½ miles Howard(Watford) led the field from Lindsell (Portsmouth) and Baker(Walton). Ken Miller was now 29th, John Thresher 50th, Derek Crookes 92nd and Jim Radford 107th; Trevor Hart being forced to drop back a considerable way with trouble from a shoulder ailment.

The race was won by Roath of Walton(56:11)from Goode of Epsom with Baker of Horsham 3rd. Walker(59:28 9th),Moore(60.49,13th), and E.Bishop (62:12,16th) completed our scoring trio and they managed to snatch 3rd place from S.L.H. in what was a desperately close finish.
Dave King came through well followed by Pat Duncan. Without Farley, Baker, Cameron or Picton it was left to John Keown to bring the team in fourth.

Hall, Bonser, Mathews, Baker, etc. - a band of stalwarts who with Lionel have travelled many expensive miles this season to take part in some gruelling events and have made sure that Belgrave has been represented far and near.

2.0 ALL OUR YESTERDAYS Tom Carter Edward Stimpson Tom Morell Ernie Duffett George Chantler 7.45 TOP TEAM Macdonald, Baker, Piddington Plummer. 10.0 LATE NIGHT EXTRA or NIGHT RIDE with Peter Hillier & Company

Others forced to withdraw were Hilton, Baker, Paget, Laws and Fairfield. The organisation was as excellent as usual and Gordon Biscoe now becomes our longest serving race secretary for this promotion with six consecutive efforts, one ahead of Arthur Whitehead who initiated the event 21 years ago.

In hot-blooded Anglo-Saxon his rivals are decried and with arms waving and eyes glittering he will spit out threats to that "*****bald headed old ***** Baker" and anyone else who dares to suggest that they will beat him next time out.
To go to the head of the field and win the race and to be acclaimed with the names of Whitlock, Baker, Thompson, Pamich, Middleton is something extra.
